item.title: Prediction Markets and States Clashed, Setting Off a Furious Political Battle
item.description: A legal dispute over the future of Kalshi, Polymarket and others has drawn in the Trump administration, the president’s son and nearly every state attorney general.
item.dc:creator: David Yaffe-Bellany and Sharon LaFraniere
item.media:credit: Ricardo Tomás

item.title: Meta Projected It Could Spend $10 Billion on Anthropic’s A.I.
item.description: The social networking giant projected it could spend $10 billion annually on Anthropic’s tools, illustrating the friend-foe relationships underlying the A.I. race.
item.dc:creator: Eli Tan and Kalley Huang

item.title: Mark Zuckerberg Wants to Make Sure YouTube and TikTok Share His Pain
item.description: Meta, the social media giant, agreed to change the way children interact with its apps. That could be trouble if its competitors don’t abide by the same rules.
item.dc:creator: Mike Isaac
item.media:credit: Anna Barclay/Getty Images
item.media:description: To settle the suits, Meta agreed to drastically rein in children’s’ access to marquee products like Instagram and Facebook.

item.title: Nvidia’s Profit Doubles to $59.69 Billion Thanks to A.I. Spending
item.description: Quarterly revenue also more than doubled, to $96.22 billion, the company said, topping expectations on Wall Street.
item.dc:creator: Kalley Huang
item.media:credit: Manuel Orbegozo for The New York Times
item.media:description: Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s chief executive, made a big bet years ago on chips and software for artificial intelligence.

item.title: Social Media and the Myth of the Big Tobacco Moment
item.description: Smoking used to be everywhere, the way Facebook, TikTok, Snap, YouTube and Instagram are now. Society decided to break the habit, but it took a long time.
item.dc:creator: David Streitfeld
item.media:credit: Jason Henry for The New York Times
item.media:description: Meta will pay up to $17.1 billion over a decade and make changes to its social media properties to make them less compulsive for young people.

item.title: Why Countries Are Pushing Social Media Bans Despite Their Flaws
item.description: Proposals for curbing social media use among children have wide support, but critics say they are ineffective.
item.dc:creator: John Yoon
item.media:credit: Jeremy Piper/Reuters
item.media:description: Teenagers in Australia on their phones. The country’s social media ban, which took effect in December, has so far failed to keep children off the platforms.

item.title: Meta Shifts the Blame + Do Data Center Bans Work? + The Final HatGPT
item.description: Meta negotiated an unusual provision in their landmark settlement: If TikTok and YouTube also agree to penalties and changes to their products, Meta will pay more.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Roose, Casey Newton, Rachel Cohn, Whitney Jones, Vjeran Pavic, Alyssa Moxley, Dan Powell, Elisheba Ittoop, Marion Lozano and Rowan Niemisto
item.media:credit: Photo Illustration by The New York Times; Image: Getty Images

item.title: Trump Administration’s Blacklisting of Anthropic Was Illegal, Judge Rules
item.description: The government retaliated against the A.I. start-up “for constitutionally protected expressive activities,” a federal judge in California wrote.
item.dc:creator: Sheera Frenkel
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:credit: Karsten Moran for The New York Times
item.media:description: Anthropic, led by Dario Amodei, was barred from government work after it insisted that its technology not be used in mass surveillance of Americans or for autonomous lethal weapons.

item.title: What Meta’s $17 Billion Settlement Means
item.description: Our reporter Cecilia Kang explains Meta’s settlement of a lawsuit claiming that the company’s social media platforms had harmed teenage users.
item.dc:creator: Cecilia Kang, Nikolay Nikolov, Paul Abowd, Alexandra Ostasiewicz and June Kim

item.title: OpenAI and 100 Others Warn That Window to Defend Against A.I. Attacks Is Narrowing
item.description: In an open letter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and others said that a wave of A.I.-enabled cyberattacks was coming and that organizations and governments needed to prepare themselves.
item.dc:creator: Kate Conger
item.media:credit: Anna Rose Layden/Reuters
item.media:description: Sam Altman of OpenAI, which has joined more than 100 tech companies in publishing an open letter warning of a wave of cyberattacks driven by artificial intelligence.

item.title: “Anxious Generation” Author Jonathan Haidt on the Meta Settlement
item.description: In “The Anxious Generation,” he laid out the evils of social media for kids. The landmark Meta settlement seems to agree.
item.dc:creator: Emma Goldberg
item.media:credit: Lila Barth for The New York Times
item.media:description: Jonathan Haidt’s 2024 book on the harms to children from social media was a best seller.

item.title: California Lawmakers Pass Plug-In Solar Bill
item.description: Legislatures in nearly a dozen states have voted to legalize use of the technology, which can help homeowners reduce their rising electricity costs.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Penn
item.media:credit: Poppy Lynch for The New York Times
item.media:description: A plug-in solar panel on the balcony of a home in Sunnyvale, Calif.

item.title: Some Scientists Have ‘Magic Hands’ in the Lab. This A.I. Is Learning Why.
item.description: Even the most adept researchers may not know exactly what they do to get successful results. An A.I. model is trying to figure it out by watching every move.
item.dc:creator: Carl Zimmer
item.media:credit: Ann Hermes for The New York Times

item.title: What’s Changing For Teens on Instagram and Facebook After Meta Settlement
item.description: Meta agreed to set more time limits and enhance protections in its platforms for young users, but was short on some specifics.
item.dc:creator: Eli Tan
item.media:credit: William West/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: Meta said that it would change how teenagers use Instagram and Facebook as part of a landmark settlement with 47 states.

item.title: What Does $17.1 Billion Mean for Meta?
item.description: The Silicon Valley company agreed to pay up to $17.1 billion in penalties as part of a landmark settlement with states over social media addiction claims.
item.dc:creator: Emmy Martin
item.media:credit: Jason Henry for The New York Times
item.media:description: Meta’s entire stock value stands at $1.45 trillion. The $17.1 billion penalty is about 1 percent of that.

item.title: Meta to Pay Up to $17.1 Billion in Landmark Settlement Over Social Media Addiction Claims
item.description: The social media giant settled with 47 states, the District of Columbia and U.S. territories, and agreed to make major changes to its products over claims its platforms endangered children.
item.dc:creator: Cecilia Kang and Eli Tan
item.media:credit: Jason Henry for The New York Times
item.media:description: Meta headquarters in California.

item.title: Bill Gates Is Warning That A.I. Is More Dangerous Than Big Tech Will Admit
item.description: In an hourlong interview, he said his industry was downplaying the risks, which he believes include mass unemployment and bioterrorism.
item.dc:creator: Karen Weise
item.media:credit: Chona Kasinger for The New York Times
item.media:description: Bill Gates is the latest in a string of tech luminaries to call out the risks of artificial intelligence.

item.title: Gold, Flights, Cryptocurrency: U.S. Vows to Go After More Than Iran’s Oil
item.description: The United States threatened sanctions for any country or entity that engages with Iran’s gold, digital assets, aviation, shipping and tech industries. Here’s why that matters.
item.dc:creator: Zane Irwin
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Vahid Salemi/Associated Press
item.media:description: A gas station in Tehran on Tuesday. The United States imposed a monthslong blockade on Iran’s shipments of oil, the nation’s economic engine.

item.title: Instagram Chief Says ‘No Silver Bullets’ for Teen Safety in Bellwether Trial
item.description: Adam Mosseri testified in a case brought by states that claim the Meta-owned app created addictive features to hook young users.
item.dc:creator: Emmy Martin and Cecilia Kang
item.media:credit: Karl Mondon/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: Adam Mosseri, the chief executive of Instagram, arriving at federal court in Oakland, Calif., on Tuesday.

item.title: SpaceX to Spend $100 Billion on Spaceport in Louisiana
item.description: It would be the rocket company’s second private launch site after Starbase, its headquarters in South Texas.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Mac
item.media:credit: Edmund D. Fountain for The New York Times
item.media:description: Gov. Jeff Landry of Louisiana during an event on Tuesday with SpaceX announcing a deal to build a spaceport in his state.

item.title: E.P.A. Moves to Curb Public Input on Air Pollution Permits for Data Centers
item.description: Under the proposal, states would no longer need to provide public notice or solicit comments on air pollution permits for data centers and other projects.
item.dc:creator: Maxine Joselow
item.media:credit: Paul Ratje for The New York Times
item.media:description: New homes in a neighborhood on the edge of an enormous Meta A.I. data center under construction in northeast El Paso last month.

item.title: Why Irregular’s A.I. Tests for Meta, Anthropic and OpenAI Went Off the Rails
item.description: Irregular, an Israeli start-up, worked with OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta to assess the security of their A.I. models. It made a mistake. Then the tests went off the rails.
item.dc:creator: Sheera Frenkel
item.media:credit: Victor Arce

item.title: Laptop Fire on American Airlines Flight Injures at Least One Passenger
item.description: Flight attendants used a fireproof bag to contain the computer after its lithium battery began smoking. One passenger was treated on the ground for injuries.
item.dc:creator: Christine Chung
item.media:credit: Caroline Brehman/EPA, via Shutterstock
item.media:description: Flight attendants acted quickly to stop a laptop fire on Friday evening aboard an American Airlines flight from Atlanta to Dallas-Fort Worth.

item.title: After Hugging Face Was Attacked By A.I. Agents, It Embarked on a Crusade
item.description: Hugging Face, a start-up that was breached by rogue bots from OpenAI, is using the hack to push for openness in A.I. development.
item.dc:creator: Kate Conger
item.media:credit: Brennan Smart for The New York Times
item.media:description: Clément Delangue, the chief executive of Hugging Face, which is a vocal supporter of open-source artificial intelligence.

item.title: How Big Tech Captured American Schools
item.description: Companies like Google and Microsoft have used their money, their might and their massive reach to influence nearly every step of the education supply chain.
item.dc:creator: Natasha Singer

item.title: Four Years Ago, a Crypto Boss Went Missing. Now His Successor Has.
item.description: The mysterious collapse of a European cryptocurrency exchange helps to explain why the industry hasn’t shaken off its reputation as a magnet for criminals.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Higgins
item.media:credit: Maciek Nabrdalik for The New York Times
item.media:description: Nicole Suszek last month with a phone showing a missing-person poster for her older brother, Sylwester Suszek.

item.title: What if Your Texts Traveled as Slowly as a Carrier Pigeon?
item.description: Apps that let users send digital messages at ultraslow speeds have taken off, with users reveling in a slower pace of life. (Just don’t use the them to make dinner plans.)
item.dc:creator: Emmett Lindner
item.media:credit: Getty Images

item.title: Anthropic Could Aim to Raise $100 Billion in Blockbuster I.P.O.
item.description: The offering could value the five-year-old A.I. start-up at $2 trillion, its bankers have told potential investors, which would exceed Elon Musk’s SpaceX.
item.dc:creator: Sri Muppidi, Lauren Hirsch and Erin Griffith
item.media:credit: Don Feria/Associated Press

item.title: TikTok Settles With U.S. Over Child Privacy Concerns for $400 Million
item.description: The Justice Department resolved a lawsuit that accused the social media company of illegally gathering children’s information.
item.dc:creator: David McCabe
item.media:credit: Anna Barclay/Getty Images
item.media:description: The government’s 2024 suit claimed that TikTok gathered data from users under the age of 13 without parental permission.

item.title: Mark Zuckerberg Buys an Irish Castle
item.description: The prominent landowner has added a nearly 200-year-old estate to his holdings. Archival information says it can take “a brisk walk of 4½ minutes to reach the dining room from the kitchen.”
item.dc:creator: Alan Yuhas
item.media:credit: Patrick Kenealy, via Reuters
item.media:description: Strancally Castle in Waterford, Ireland, was built around 1830 and renovated in the early 2000s. It now belongs to Mark Zuckerberg.
